rounds.text: Him Teknoforge Ltd trades at an attractive valuation discount across multiple core metrics compared to its industry peers [E5]. Specifically, the company commands a price-to-earnings multiple of 22.39x against a sector benchmark of 24.9x [E5]. Furthermore, the enterprise value to EBITDA ratio stands at a compelling 9.48x, offering a favorable discount relative to the sector benchmark of 12.34x [E10]. Asset backing is equally pronounced, with the price-to-book ratio sitting at 1.16x compared to a much higher sector benchmark of 3x [E6]. The market price also reflects steady underlying momentum, currently positioned 71% of the way up its 52-week range between a low of 177 and a high of 298 [E4]. Conceded: [E21], [E22], [E23], [E41], and [E42].

The bull’s reliance on sector benchmarks [E5, E6, E10] ignores the company’s fundamental inability to generate efficient returns, as evidenced by an ROE of 5.17% compared to the 11.88% sector average [E8]. This poor capital efficiency is further highlighted by an ROA of 2.48%, which is less than half of the 6.33% sector benchmark [E7]. While the bull cites a P/E of 22.39x [E5], this figure is contradicted by the company’s own filed statements showing a P/E of 33.9 [E1], suggesting the stock is significantly more expensive than the bull claims. The market price of 263 is fundamentally detached from intrinsic value, as the DCF analysis indicates a value of only 154 [E21], resulting in a negative margin of safety of 71.1% [E22]. Furthermore, the current price assumes an aggressive 17.3% earnings growth rate, far exceeding the 10.0% base case expectation [E23]. Conceded: [E4], [E5], [E6], [E10].

scorecard.note: Computed arithmetically from the citations that survived grounding — no model input.

evidence.fact: The stock sits 71% of the way up its 52-week range (177 low to 298 high).
P/E of 22.39x against a sector benchmark of 24.9x.
P/B of 1.16x against a sector benchmark of 3x.
ROA of 2.48% against a sector benchmark of 6.33%.
ROE of 5.17% against a sector benchmark of 11.88%.
EV/EBITDA of 9.48x against a sector benchmark of 12.34x.
A discounted cash flow puts intrinsic value at Rs 154 per share against a market price of Rs 263.
That leaves a margin of safety of -71.1%.
A reverse DCF says today's price already implies 17.3% earnings growth, against the 10.0% the base case assumes.
Bias check — Valuation blind-spot: Rich valuation — P/E 34, DCF overvalued 71%. A market-beating chart doesn't make a rich entry safe; the price already discounts a lot of the good news.
